newsitem.title: TAIWAN: POLL-TAIWAN Q2 CURRENT ACCOUNT SEEN LOWER SURPLUS.
newsitem.headline: POLL-TAIWAN Q2 CURRENT ACCOUNT SEEN LOWER SURPLUS.

text.p: A Reuters Poll of Taiwan economists on Thursday projected a surplus of US$1.314 billion for the second-quarter current account, compared with a surplus of US$1.992 billion in the second-quarter 1996.
Official figures are tentatively scheduled to be released by the central bank after 0800 GMT on August 20.
The first-quarter current account showed a surplus of US$1.928 billion.
The following table lists institutions' forecasts for Taiwan current account in the second quarter, in billions of U.S. dollars. ( ) indicates deficit if any.
Current account mainly includes merchandise, services and income balance, as well as current transfers.
Taiwan in recent years usually has a surplus in merchandise and income, but deficit in services and current transfers.

Economists said the second-quarter trade surplus, which fell 41 percent year-on-year to US$1.81 billion, is expected to contribute to a lower current account surplus in the second quarter compared with a year earlier.

"Import growth had recently risen more than export growth, resulting a dwindling merchandise trade surplus and thus dragging down the current account surplus," said Nomura Securities economist Amy Huang.
